first.rationale: The immediate competitive loss is concentrated in price-sensitive SMBs, where targeted promotional pricing previously produced strong acquisition and revenue lift. A small, tightly targeted test can address that threat while limiting discounting, margin, and longer-term willingness-to-pay risks. Onboarding deterioration remains material, so memory_86 is requested to validate whether its durable activation benefit should outweigh the more immediate pricing response.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified source record showed completion up 13%, time-to-value down 2.1 days, and 30-day retention up 3%, directly addressing the 4% completion decline and plausibly helping the concurrent activation decline. This is more consistent with sustainable qualified revenue than promotional pricing: its verified 18% qualified-revenue lift came with 30-day retention down 12% and an explicit warning against treating discounting as sustainable growth. Use a controlled experiment rather than a broad rollout to confirm effect size in the current cohort and monitor qualified revenue and retention alongside completion and activation.

final2.rationale: Continue with the onboarding-simplification experiment rather than react with deeper promotional pricing. Verified onboarding evidence directly supports durable completion, time-to-value, and retention improvement, while the verified pricing experiment generated a 12% 30-day retention decline and explicitly was not sustainable. The escalated competitor move raises near-term SMB churn risk, so track price-sensitive SMB retention and qualified revenue as guardrails; however, it does not establish that discounting will preserve long-term qualified revenue.
